newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Electric to raise tariffs by 3.47 pct.
newsitem.headline: HK Electric to raise tariffs by 3.47 pct.

text.p: Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd unit Hongkong Electric Co Ltd said on Monday it would raise its average net tariff by 3.47 percent or 2.9 Hong Kong cents per kWh, with effect from January.
The increase was due to inflationary pressure in Hong Kong, the firm said in a statement.

It said inflation in the territory, as measured by the Consumer Price Index (A), had gone up by more than 180 percent since January 1983 compared with a 43 percent rise in the electricity net tariff during the same period.
That represented a 49 percent reduction in the electricity net tariff in real terms, it said.
The last tariff rise, a 3.9 percent increase, was made in January 1996.
The company generates and supplies electricity to parts of Hong Kong, including Hong Kong island.
